title: Comunicado 2025-05-29
summary: The SARB MPC cut the repo rate by 25bp to 7.25%, with five members in favour and one preferring a 50bp cut, on a benign inflation picture (headline below 3%, core at the bottom of the range, forecasts revised down on fuel, a firmer rand and the cancelled VAT hike) and weaker growth. The baseline projection has rates broadly flat above 7% after this cut, but the Committee said it prefers a 3% inflation-objective scenario in which the policy rate falls to just under 6%, and sees scope to 'clear the way for sustainably lower interest rates', a conditional path to further easing tied to lower inflation expectations. Versus the March statement, which held rates with two members wanting a cut, saw medium-term inflation risks skewed to the upside and called for a cautious approach, the Committee moved to a cut, now sees balanced risks to inflation and growth, and the lone dissent is on the dovish side. The adverse rand-depreciation scenario remains as the hawkish caveat.

key_quotes.quote: Against this backdrop, the MPC decided to reduce the policy rate by 25 basis points, with effect from 30 May. Five members favoured this action, while one preferred a cut of 50 basis points.
key_quotes.context: Decision and vote: 25bp cut, one dissent for a larger cut

key_quotes.quote: The policy rate falls to just under 6%, rather than staying above 7%, as in the baseline.
key_quotes.context: 3% objective scenario implies a much lower rate path than the flat baseline

key_quotes.quote: The SARB’s main contribution is to deliver price stability, and we see scope to lock in low inflation and clear the way for sustainably lower interest rates.
key_quotes.context: Framing of lower target as a route to lower rates

key_quotes.quote: Core inflation came in at 3%, at the bottom of our target range.
key_quotes.context: Underlying inflation well contained; risks to the forecast balanced
